title: Character Polynomials, FI-Modules, and Representation Stability

items.title: The category FI and FI-modules over a commutative ring
items.statement: Let $FI$ be the category whose objects are the finite sets and whose morphisms are the injections ([[def-category]]); it is equivalent to the full subcategory on the objects $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, $n\ge0$, so that $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])\cong S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]). An **FI-module over a commutative ring $k$** ([[def-commutative-ring]]) is a covariant functor $V\colon FI\to k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]); write $V_S=V(S)$, $V_n=V([n])$ and $f_*=V(f)$ for a morphism $f$. Since $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])=S_n$, the maps $V_n\to V_n$ induced by permutations make $V_n$ a left $kS_n$-module ([[def-group-ring]]), and each $f_*\colon V_m\to V_n$ is equivariant for the conjugation homomorphism $S_m\to S_n$ determined by $f$. A **sub-FI-module** of $V$ is a subfunctor of $V$ ([[def-submodule]]), a **map of FI-modules** is a natural transformation, and kernels, images and cokernels are computed pointwise, so the FI-modules over $k$ inherit an abelian-category structure from $k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-quotient-module]]). An **FB-module** over $k$ is a functor from the groupoid $FB$ of finite sets and bijections to $k\text{-Mod}$; an FB-module is determined up to isomorphism by the $kS_n$-modules $W_n$ and carries no transition maps.
items.strategy: Read complete Definition and all eleven suppliers. Full skeletal inclusion and existence of individual finite-set bijections require no simultaneous class choice; the equivariance homomorphism extends permutations by the identity off the image. Kernels/cokernels and coimage-image isomorphisms are objectwise. S_0 and the zero ring cause no failure. Accept the clarified skeletal formulation; subsequent FI consumers use only these explicit constructions.

items.title: Span, finite generation and generation degree of an FI-module
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ and let $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ be a set of elements. The **sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of $V$ containing $\Sigma$; it is the smallest such sub-FI-module and consists of all finite $k$-linear combinations of elements $f_*(v)$ with $v\in\Sigma$ and $f$ a morphism of $FI$. Call $V$ **finitely generated** when $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$ for some finite $\Sigma$, and **generated in degree $\le d$** when $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le d})=V$, where $V_{\le d}=\bigsqcup_{|S|\le d}V_S$; the **generation degree** is the least such $d$, and $\infty$ when no such $d$ exists ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]). Finite generation of $V$ and pointwise finite generation of the $k$-modules $V_S$ are different conditions: the latter is implied by the former ([[lem-generated-in-degree-d-is-a-quotient-of-free-fi-modules]]) but does not imply it, and no pointwise finite-dimensionality is built into either notion ([[def-submodule]] for the span).
items.strategy: Read Definition and all four suppliers. Intersections exist objectwise and equal the explicit finite-linear-combination span of all generator images. Skeletal V_<=d is set-sized; individual finite transports suffice. The empty generating set generates zero with degree zero, and finite generators imply a bounded maximum of support sizes. Bounded degree permits infinite low-rank modules and does not assert finite generation. Accept corrected set-sized family and finite maximum.

items.title: The coinvariant functors $\Phi_a$ and the transition maps $T$
items.statement:
A **graded $k[T]$-module** consists of $k$-modules $U_n$, $n\ge0$, together
with $k$-linear maps $T=T_n\colon U_n\to U_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge0$. A
**morphism** $U\to U'$ of graded $k[T]$-modules is a family of $k$-linear maps
$u_n\colon U_n\to U'_n$ with $u_{n+1}\circ T_n=T'_n\circ u_n$ for all $n$.

Fix $a\ge0$, a set $\mathbf a$ of cardinality $a$, and a functorial disjoint
union of finite sets. Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]) and let $n\ge0$. Put

$$\Phi_a(V)_n:=(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n},$$

the coinvariants of the $kS_n$-module $V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$: the quotient by
the span of the elements $\sigma\cdot v-v$, $\sigma\in S_n$, $v\in
V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]],
[[def-quotient-module]]). Equivalently $\Phi_a(V)_n=k\otimes_{kS_n}
V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$, the two descriptions being identified by the balancing
argument of [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]] and
the corresponding identification for $\mathbb Z$ in
[[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]]; the group ring $kS_n$ is a
unital $k$-algebra with basis the group elements
([[def-group-ring]], [[thm-group-ring-is-a-unital-algebra-with-basis-g]]).

To define the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$, choose an
injection $f\colon n\to n+1$. It induces the injection
$\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f\colon\mathbf a\sqcup n\to\mathbf a\sqcup n+1$
and hence a $k$-linear map $(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}\to
V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n+1})$. This map is $S_n$-equivariant, where $S_n$ acts on
the target through the injection $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f$, so it
descends to the quotient map $T=T_f$ on coinvariants. The map $T_f$ is
independent of $f$: for two injections $f,g\colon n\to n+1$ the composite
$g\circ f^{-1}$ is a bijection $f(n)\to g(n)$, which extends along the
complement to a permutation $\tau\in S_{n+1}$ with $g=\tau\circ f$; then
$\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup g=(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup
\tau)\circ(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f)$, and the map induced by
$\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup\tau$ on
$(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n+1})_{S_{n+1}}$ is the identity because it comes from
the action of the group element $\tau$. Thus $T$ is well defined and
$(\Phi_a(V),T)$ is a graded $k[T]$-module.

A map of FI-modules $\alpha\colon V\to W$ gives $k$-linear maps
$\alpha_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}\colon V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}\to W_{\mathbf
a\sqcup n}$ commuting with the $S_n$-actions and with the maps induced by
$\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f$, hence maps $(\Phi_a\alpha)_n$ of coinvariants
commuting with $T$; so $\Phi_a$ is a functor from FI-modules over $k$ to graded
$k[T]$-modules.

Permutations of $\mathbf a$ commute with the moving-block action of $S_n$,
so $\Phi_a(V)_n$ also carries an $S_a$-action. Since
$\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f$ commutes with these permutations, every $T$
is $S_a$-equivariant. Naturality has the same equivariance.

**Exactness.** Coinvariants of a group module are right exact
([[prop-the-coinvariants-functor-is-right-exact]]), so the functor
$M\mapsto M_{S_n}\cong k\otimes_{kS_n}M$ is right exact and each $\Phi_a$ is
right exact in every degree. If $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$, then $1/n!$ exists in $k$
and the averaging map
$s\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$,
$s([v])=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\sigma\cdot v$, is a well-defined
$k$-linear section of the quotient map that is natural in $V$; it identifies
$\Phi_a(V)_n$ with the invariants $V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}^{S_n}$. Under this
natural identification $\Phi_a$ becomes the invariants functor, which is left
exact (kernels of equivariant maps are computed pointwise), and therefore
$\Phi_a$ is exact; in that case the induced map $\Phi_a(W)\to\Phi_a(V)$ is
injective for every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$
([[def-submodule]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]), so
$\Phi_a(W)$ is identified with a submodule of $\Phi_a(V)$. Finite averaging
uses only the finite groups $S_n$; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Choice-independence of $T$: the two injections differ by a permutation of $n+1$, and coinvariants identify the images. Functoriality and right exactness are pointwise from the right-exact coinvariant functor; left exactness over a $\mathbb Q$-algebra follows because $(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n}\to V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ is split by the averaging map $v\mapsto\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\sigma v$, which is defined when $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ and is natural ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]).

items.title: Injectivity, surjectivity and stability degree
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. The **injectivity degree** $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)$ (respectively the **surjectivity degree** $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$) is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective (respectively surjective) for all $n\ge s$; the **stability degree** is $$\operatorname{stab-deg}(V):=\max\bigl(\operatorname{inj-deg}(V),\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\bigr).$$ Each of the three is $+\infty$ when no such $s$ exists. Equivalently, $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism for all $a\ge0$ and all $n\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. The three bounds are kept distinct: stability degree is the max, and injectivity and surjectivity degree need not agree in examples.
items.strategy: Unwrap the definitions ($\max$ of two extended nonnegative integers), and record the equivalent indexing statement as a reformulation: $T$ is an isomorphism iff it is both injective and surjective, and each of the two stated bounds is the least threshold controlling the corresponding property. No claim of finiteness is made; $\infty$ is allowed throughout.

items.title: Specht modules classify the irreducibles over every field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $n\ge0$. The field-valued Specht modules $S^\lambda_F$, $\lambda\vdash n$, of [[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] are nonzero, irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, and every irreducible $F S_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them; consequently, by Maschke, every finite-dimensional $F S_n$-module is a direct sum of copies of the $S^\lambda_F$, so the irreducible $F S_n$-modules are indexed by the partitions of $n$ and the $S^\lambda_F$ form a complete irredundant list. This is the constituent convention used throughout the pair: over $F=\mathbb C$ it specialises to the published complex classification, and over a general characteristic-zero field F it is proved using rational Specht models and extension Q -> F, not a scalar extension from C to F.
items.strategy: Use the rational Specht models, then extend from the prime field, never from an arbitrary field to C. The integral standard basis gives explicit matrices with rational entries on S^lambda_Q and an isomorphism F tensor_Q S^lambda_Q = S^lambda_F for every characteristic-zero field F. Over Q, a proper nonzero invariant subspace would remain proper and nonzero under the explicit finite-dimensional extension Q -> C, contradicting complex irreducibility. For finite-dimensional rational representations, equivariant Hom spaces are kernels of finite rational matrices; matrix ranks are unchanged on extension to C. Thus End_QSn(S^lambda_Q)=Q and Hom_QSn(S^lambda_Q,S^mu_Q)=0 for lambda!=mu. Any simple QSn-module W is finite-dimensional (a nonzero w generates it as a quotient of QSn); its complex extension has a Specht constituent, and the same Hom-rank comparison descends a nonzero map S^lambda_Q -> W, proving completeness over Q. Maschke therefore decomposes the finite regular module QSn as a finite sum of rational Specht modules. Extend this finite decomposition along Q -> F. The same rational Hom-matrix ranks give End_FSn(S^lambda_F)=F and zero Hom between distinct shapes; Maschke implies each S^lambda_F is irreducible, since a proper summand would give a non-scalar projection. Every simple FSn-module is a quotient of the regular module, so the extended decomposition proves completeness over F. All scalar extensions and rank comparisons concern explicit finite-dimensional matrices, not an embedding F -> C. No arbitrary-index choice is used.

items.title: Weight of an FI-module over a field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$, the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), and let $V(\lambda)_n$ denote the irreducible $kS_n$-module indexed by the partition $\lambda[n]$, i.e. $k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$, the scalar extension of its rational Specht model ([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]], [[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]). The **weight** of $V$ is $$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\},$$ the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed; it is $0$ for $V=0$ and $+\infty$ when the set is unbounded. If $W$ is a subquotient of $V$ then $\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: every partition of $n$ is uniquely $\lambda[n]$ for a partition $\lambda$ (the boxes below the first row form a partition), so the constituent labels are well defined and the supremum is over a set of nonnegative integers. The subquotient inequality is immediate since constituents of a subquotient are constituents of $V$. The item records the convention that $k$ may be any characteristic-zero field via the absolute irreducibility supplied by the classification lemma; no finiteness of $\operatorname{weight}(V)$ is asserted. Constituent tests require no basis or global decomposition for infinite-dimensional values: every vector has a finite-dimensional orbit span under the finite group, and finite-dimensional Maschke applies there. A finite-dimensional submodule of a quotient can be lifted into a finite-dimensional orbit-stable subspace using finitely many vector lifts; this gives the stated subquotient monotonicity without infinite choices.

items.title: The free FI-module $M(W)$ generated by an $S_m$-module
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$, i.e. a family of $kS_m$-modules $W_m$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). The **free FI-module** $M(W)$ is the FI-module with $$M(W)_S:=\bigoplus_{T\subseteq S}W_T,$$ where $W_T$ denotes $W_{|T|}$ transported along a bijection $T\to[|T|]$ (well defined up to canonical isomorphism), and on an injection $f\colon S\to S'$ the map $M(W)_S\to M(W)_{S'}$ is the sum of the maps $W_T\to W_{f(T)}$ induced by $f|_T$ ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). $M(-)$ is the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from FI-modules to FB-modules, so $$\operatorname{Hom}_{FI\text{-}Mod}(M(W),V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{FB\text{-}Mod}(W,\pi V)$$ naturally in $V$; the unit sends $W_S$ to the summand $W_S$ of $M(W)_S$. As an $S_n$-module, $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ with $\boxtimes$ the external tensor product of modules for the direct factors and $\operatorname{Ind}$ the induced module built from $H$-covariant functions ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]], [[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]). For $m\ge0$, $M(m):=M(k[S_m])$ has as a $k$-basis the injections $m\to S$; for a partition $\lambda$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, $M(\lambda):=M(S^\lambda_k)$.
items.strategy: Read Definition, ten suppliers and finite-index induction comparison. Subset summands and restriction-of-injection maps compose; degree grouping has stabilizer S_a x S_(n-a), acting through W_a and a trivial complementary factor. Finite-index covariant functions and the tensor induction model agree here. Adjunction extensions on subset inclusions are inverse; M(m) is injection representable, including M(0)=constant k. No classwide transports are chosen. The raw carrier changed, but both pre/post contract and substantive construction are unchanged; review records metadata normalization.

items.title: Generation in bounded degree presents an FI-module as a quotient of free FI-modules
items.statement:
Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]), with free FI-modules $M(m)$ as in
[[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]] and span as in
[[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]].

(a) For $v\in V_m$ the map of FI-modules $M(m)\to V$ sending the canonical
generator $\mathrm{id}_m\in M(m)_m$ to $v$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(v)$;
more generally, for any set $\Sigma$ of elements, each lying in some $V_S$, the
canonical map $\bigoplus_{s\in\Sigma}M(S_s)\to V$ sending $\mathrm{id}_{S_s}$
to $s$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$. Here $S_s$ is the specified
supporting set of $s$, and $M(S)_T$ is the free $k$-module on injections
$S\to T$, with postcomposition as transition maps. Each $M(S)$ is
isomorphic to $M(|S|)$ after choosing a single bijection $[|S|]\to S$.

(b) $V$ is finitely generated if and only if there is a finite family
$m_1,\dots,m_r\ge0$ with a surjection

$$M(m_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus M(m_r)\twoheadrightarrow V;$$

$V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ if and only if there is a surjection
$\bigoplus_{i\in I}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ with $m_i\le d$ for all $i$. In
particular, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then the evaluation map
$\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\to V$, whose value on a summand $V_T$ supported on an $m$-element subset
$T\subseteq S$ is the transition map $V_T\to V_S$, is surjective.

(c) If $V$ is finitely generated, then $V_S$ is a finitely generated $k$-module
for every finite set $S$
([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]).

No choice principle is used: all maps come from a finite or explicitly indexed
set of generators, and the image computations are linear algebra on the values
at a fixed finite set.
items.strategy: Read all six steps and six suppliers. Representable M(S) maps basis injections to transition images, avoiding simultaneous transports for arbitrary generator sets. Skeletal bounded generation yields a possibly infinite sum of M(m), while finite generation uses finitely many transports and finitely many M(m). Evaluation M(V_m) is separately the adjunction map and is surjective. Fixed finite sets have finite injection bases, proving pointwise finite generation. Empty generator sum gives zero; d=0 gives constant representables. Accepted mathematical repairs and amended the family length from k to r throughout Statement and Proof, resolving refuter:18:3 without changing the coefficient ring.

items.title: Free FI-modules have computable stability degree and weight
items.statement:
Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$ and let $M(W)$ be the free FI-module of
[[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]]. Then
$\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for all $i>m$ then
$\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular
$M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ over a nonzero ring $k$ satisfies $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$
([[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition,
then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]) and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: The displayed computation of $\Phi_aM(W)$ as $\bigoplus_{U\subseteq\mathbf a,0\le j\le n}\Phi_{|U|}(W)_j$ shows that $T$ preserves the summands and acts as the identity on each, giving injectivity degree $0$; when $W$ vanishes above $m$ the $j$-range is exhausted for $n\ge m$, giving surjectivity degree $\le m$, and $\Phi_0(k[S_m])_m\cong k$ gives the exact value $m$ for $M(m)$. For M(lambda), branching for Ind_{S_m x S_{n-m}}^{S_n}(S^lambda x k) gives full shapes nu obtained by adding n-m boxes in distinct columns. Hence nu_1>=n-m, so the padding-tail size n-nu_1 is at most m; equality is attained for the padded shape lambda[n] when n>=m+lambda_1. For exact stability, Phi_a M(S^lambda)_n decomposes into factors (S^lambda)_{S_j}, indexed by subsets U of [a] with |U|+j=m and j<=n. Transition T is the identity on existing factors. By branching, (S^lambda)_{S_j}=0 for j>lambda_1, so no new nonzero factor appears after n=lambda_1; the factor j=lambda_1 is nonzero, and with a=m-lambda_1 and U=[a] it first appears there. Thus T fails surjectivity at n=lambda_1-1 if lambda_1>0, proving stability degree exactly lambda_1; for the empty partition it is zero.

items.title: Bounded generation degree bounds surjectivity degree and weight
items.statement:
Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$, with surjectivity degree and stability degree
as in [[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]] and
weight as in [[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]].

(a) Every quotient $V\twoheadrightarrow W$ of FI-modules satisfies
$\operatorname{surj-deg}(W)\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$.

(b) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$
([[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]] is the source of the
notation), then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le d$.

(c) If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $V$ is generated in
degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: (a) $\Phi_a$ is right exact, so $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(W)_n$ is surjective in every degree and a surjective $T$ remains surjective on the quotient. (b) By the presentation lemma $V$ is a quotient of $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)$, and each summand is an $M(W)$ with $W$ supported in degrees $\le d$, so it has surjectivity degree $\le d$; a finite direct sum has surjectivity degree the maximum, and (a) passes the bound to the quotient $V$. (c) The same presentation exhibits $V$ as a quotient of $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)$, each $M(V_m)$ has weight $\le m\le d$ by the free-module bound, and weight is monotone under subquotients, so $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$. For (c), no finite-dimensionality of V_m is assumed: every finite collection of vectors in V_m lies in a finite-dimensional S_m-stable orbit span. In M(V_m)_n each vector involves only finitely many such coefficients and injections, so it lies in the induction of one finite-dimensional coefficient subrepresentation. Finite-dimensional Maschke and the branching lemma bound every simple constituent by m; finite sums and quotients preserve this bound. A finite-dimensional simple submodule of a quotient is lifted using finitely many basis vectors and their finite S_n-orbits, so no infinite-dimensional decomposition or choice of an infinite basis is needed.

items.title: Tensor products of finitely generated FI-modules are finitely generated
items.statement: Let $V$ and $W$ be finitely generated FI-modules over $k$, with pointwise tensor product $(V\otimes W)_S=V_S\otimes_k W_S$. Then $V\otimes W$ is finitely generated. More precisely, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le m_1$ and $W$ in degree $\le m_2$, then $V\otimes W$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$.
items.strategy: Read six proof steps and seven suppliers. Basis pairs factor through the union of their images, of size <=m_1+m_2; tensor right exactness and direct-sum distribution pass the bounded degree result to arbitrary-index presentations. Finite generation separately uses finite presentations and the finite union of low-rank injection pairs, so it never follows merely from bounded generation. Empty sums, zero modules/ring, m_i=0 and equal/overlapping image pairs are valid; finite transports only. Accept the repaired finite-generator argument.

items.title: Coinvariants detect vanishing of subquotients of bounded weight, and padded irreducibles stabilise
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\mu\vdash n$, and write
$\mu=\lambda[n]$ as in [[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]; set
$V(\lambda)_n:=V_\mu$, the irreducible $kS_n$-module with label $\mu$
([[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]).
Read $\mu_1=0$ when $\mu=\varnothing$. For $0\le a\le n$, put
$k_0=n-a$; for a vector space carrying an action of $S_a\times S_{k_0}$, write $(\,\cdot\,)_{S_{k_0}}$ for $S_{k_0}$-coinvariants of the
restriction to that product ([[def-fi-coinvariant-functors-and-transition-maps]]).

(i) For $a\le n$, with $k_0=n-a$, the $S_a$-representation
$(V_\mu)_{S_{k_0}}$ is zero if and only if $n-a>\mu_1$, equivalently
$(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$ if and only if $a<|\lambda|$.

(ii) If $n-a=\mu_1$ (that is, $a=|\lambda|$), then
$(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong V_\lambda$ as $S_{|\lambda|}$-modules.

(iii) For fixed $\lambda$ and $a\ge|\lambda|$, the $S_a$-module
$(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}$ is independent of $n$ once $n\ge a+\lambda_1$; in
fact $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{|\lambda|}\times
S_{a-|\lambda|}}^{S_a}(V_\lambda\boxtimes k)$ throughout that range.

(iv) If $V$ is an FI-module over $k$ with $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le a$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]), then, for every $n\ge a$, every subquotient
$W_n$ ([[def-submodule]]) of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies
$W_n=0\iff(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Apply the branching lemma part (ii) with $S^\lambda_F = V_\mu$: $(V_\mu)_{S_{n-a}}$ is the sum of the irreducibles $V_\nu$ over partitions $\nu\vdash a$ obtained from $\mu$ by removing one box from each of $n-a$ different columns; such a removal is possible iff $n-a\le\mu_1$, and when $n-a=\mu_1$ it is possible only by removing every column's bottom box, leaving $\lambda$; this gives (i) and (ii). For (iii), write m=|lambda| and mu=lambda[n]=(n-m,lambda_1,...). A partition nu of a occurs on the left precisely when mu_i>=nu_i>=mu_{i+1} for every i, by horizontal-strip removal. On the right, Pieri gives exactly nu_i>=lambda_i>=nu_{i+1}. These are the same inequalities except for nu_1<=n-m; the latter is automatic because |nu|-|lambda|=a-m gives nu_1<=lambda_1+a-m<=n-m in the stated range n>=a+lambda_1. Thus both sides have exactly the same constituents, each with multiplicity one, proving the displayed isomorphism independent of n. For (iv), if $W_n$ is nonzero, fix a nonzero vector and its finite-dimensional $S_n$-orbit span. Finite-dimensional Maschke supplies a simple submodule $V(\lambda)_n$ with $|\lambda|\le a$. By (i) its $S_{n-a}$-coinvariants are nonzero. Coinvariants over a characteristic-zero field are exact: the finite averaging operator identifies the quotient with invariants and preserves injections. Hence $(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}$ is nonzero. The reverse direction is immediate. This proves the claim even when $W_n$ is infinite-dimensional, without choosing an infinite basis or decomposition.

items.title: A stability degree bounds the first row of every padding tail
items.statement:
Read missing partition parts as $0$ when comparing row lengths.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]), and put
$s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$
([[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). Then
for every $n\ge0$, every irreducible constituent $V(\lambda)_n$ of the
$kS_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies

$$\lambda_1\le s.$$

Equivalently, since the padded partition is
$\lambda[n]=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$, the second row of the
Specht diagram $\lambda[n]$ has length at most $s$; the first row of the
padding tail is the second row of the full diagram
([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]],
[[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]). No choice principle is
used.
items.strategy:
Filter $V$ by $F^mV:=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le m})$, so that $V= igcup_mF^mV$ and each $F^mV$ is generated in degree $\le m$. It suffices to prove the bound for every constituent of every quotient $F^mV/F^{m-1}V$. Fix $m$ and let $\overline V:=V/F^{m-1}V$; then $\overline V_n=0$ for $n<m$ and $\overline V_m\cong H_m:=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le m})/\operatorname{span}(V_{<m})$ is its degree-$m$ part. If $m\le s$ then any $\mu\vdash m$ has $\mu_1\le m\le s$; for $m\ge s+1$ the index $a_0:=m-s-1$ is nonnegative: since $\overline V$ is a quotient of $V$, part (a) of the generation lemma gives $\operatorname{surj-deg}(\overline V)\le s$, so $T\colon\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_s	o\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_{s+1}$ is surjective; its domain is a quotient of $\overline V_{m-1}=0$, hence $0$; but $\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_{s+1}=(\overline V_m)_{S_{s+1}}$, so $(H_m)_{S_{s+1}}=0$, and the coinvariant lemma (i) with subgroup size $s+1$ (retained rank $m-s-1$) gives $\mu_1\le s$ for every constituent $V_\mu$ of $H_m$. Next, $F^mV/F^{m-1}V$ is generated in degree $\le m$ with vanishing values below $m$, so the presentation lemma gives a surjection $M(H_m)	woheadrightarrow F^mV/F^{m-1}V$; by the free-module description every constituent of $M(H_m)_n$ is obtained from a constituent $H_\mu$ of $H_m$ by adding boxes in different columns, giving a full diagram $
u$ with $
u_2\le\mu_1\le s$ by horizontal-strip interlacing; if $
u=\lambda[n]$, then $\lambda_1=
u_2$; a quotient of $M(H_m)_n$ has no other constituents. Passing along the filtration gives the claim for $V_n$. All constituent arguments can be made in finite-dimensional orbit spans; any constituent vector in the exhaustive filtration already occurs at a finite stage. The bound concerns the tail, not the growing first row of lambda[n].

items.title: FI-modules over a Noetherian $\mathbb Q$-algebra form a Noetherian category
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a commutative Noetherian ring containing $\mathbb Q$
([[def-noetherian-ring]], [[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]), and
let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$
([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]],
[[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). Then every sub-FI-module
$W\subseteq V$ is again finitely generated: the category of FI-modules over
$k$ is Noetherian, in the sense that every subobject of a finitely generated
object is finitely generated. The hypothesis that $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ is
used only through the exactness of the functors $\Phi_a$ and through
restriction of scalars to $\mathbb Q$
([[def-fi-coinvariant-functors-and-transition-maps]]). No choice principle is
used.
items.strategy: Let $V$ be generated in degree $\le a$ and let $W\subseteq V$. First, $V_n$ is a finitely generated $k$-module for every $n$ (presentation lemma (c)), and the graded $k[T]$-module $\Phi_a(V)$ is finitely generated: $T$ is surjective in degrees $\ge a$ by the generation-degree bound (b), so $\Phi_a(V)$ is generated over $k[T]$ by the finitely many components $\Phi_a(V)_0,\dots,\Phi_a(V)_a$, each a finitely generated $k$-module as a quotient of $V_{a+i}$. Since $k[T]$ is Noetherian ([[thm-hilbert-basis-theorem]], [[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and a finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian ([[thm-finitely-generated-modules-over-noetherian-rings-are-noetherian]], [[def-noetherian-module]]), the submodule $\Phi_a(W)\subseteq\Phi_a(V)$ is a finitely generated graded $k[T]$-module; take a finite generating set and replace each generator by its finitely many homogeneous components (the submodule is graded), obtaining homogeneous generators $x_1,\dots,x_r$, lift each $x_i\in\Phi_a(W)_{n_i}$ to $w_i\in W_{a+n_i}$, and let $\widetilde W\subseteq W$ be generated by the $w_i$ together with finite generating sets of $W_0,\dots,W_{a-1}$. Then $\Phi_a(\widetilde W)=\Phi_a(W)$, and exactness of $\Phi_a$ over $\mathbb Q$-algebras gives $\Phi_a(W/\widetilde W)=0$. It remains to show $U:=W/\widetilde W=0$. Restrict scalars from k to Q, as in the complete proof of CEF Theorem 1.3; no map k -> C is used. The evaluation surjection direct_sum_{m<=a} M_k(V_m) -> V stays surjective on restriction, and M_k(V_m)_Q = M_Q((V_m)_Q): free k-modules on finite injection sets become the same finite direct sums of rational coefficient spaces, and the S_m-balanced relations agree because the actions are k-linear. Thus V_Q is generated in degree <=a over Q, although its values can be infinite-dimensional. The generation-degree/weight supplier now proves this case through finite orbit-stable subspaces of the coefficient modules, so weight(V_Q)<=a. U_Q is a subquotient and has the same bound. Restriction commutes with coinvariants: the k-submodule generated by hv-v is exactly its Q-linear span, since c(hv-v)=h(cv)-cv for c in k. Therefore Phi_a(U_Q)=0. For every n>=a, apply the vanishing-detection supplier to U_Q,n, with averaging over the finite group S_{n-a}. Its proof uses only a finite-dimensional cyclic submodule if U_Q,n is nonzero, not a decomposition of the whole rational space. It follows that U_Q,n=0, hence U_n=0. For n<a, the chosen finite generators of W_n already give tilde W_n=W_n. Consequently W=tilde W is finitely generated. All Noetherian-module uses and all generator/lift selections are finite; the Hilbert citation uses only its explicitly choice-free ideal implication.

items.title: Uniform representation stability for consistent sequences of $S_n$-modules
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$. A **consistent sequence** is a
sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ in which each $V_n$ is a finite-dimensional
left $kS_n$-module and each $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is
$S_n$-equivariant, the target being regarded as an $S_n$-module by restriction
along the standard inclusion $S_n\hookrightarrow S_{n+1}$ that fixes $n$. An
FI-module $V$ over $k$ with finite-dimensional values
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]) determines such a sequence by
$V_n:=V([n])$ and $\varphi_n:=f_*$ for the standard inclusions
$f\colon[n]\to[n+1]$; these maps are $S_n$-equivariant by functoriality and the
conjugation action, since $f\circ\sigma=\Phi_f(\sigma)\circ f$ with
$\Phi_f(\sigma)$ the extension of $\sigma$ by the fixed point $n$.

The sequence is **uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge N$**
when all three of the following hold.

1. **(I) Injectivity.** The map $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is injective for
   every $n\ge N$.
2. **(II) Surjectivity.** The $S_{n+1}$-span of the image $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is
   all of $V_{n+1}$ for every $n\ge N$.
3. **(III) Multiplicities.** For each partition $\lambda$ and each $n$ with
   $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$, let $V(\lambda)_n$ be the irreducible $kS_n$-module
   indexed by the first-row padding $\lambda[n]=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$
   ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), namely the scalar extension
   $k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$ of the rational Specht model,
   which is the unique irreducible $kS_n$-module with that label
   ([[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]];
   over $\mathbb C$ this is the published complex Specht classification
   [[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]]). Decompose
   $V_n\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda}c_{\lambda,n}V(\lambda)_n$ with multiplicities
   $c_{\lambda,n}\ge0$, the sum over those $\lambda$ with
   $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$. Then for every fixed $\lambda$ the multiplicity
   $c_{\lambda,n}$ is independent of $n$ for all $n\ge N$, with
   $c_{\lambda,n}:=0$ when $n<|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ so that undefined
   padded modules do not leave undefined multiplicities.

The sequence is **uniformly representation stable** when it is so for some
$N\ge0$. All three conditions are part of the definition, and (II) is not a
consequence of (I) and (III): take $V_n=k^{[n]}$ with its permutation action and, for $n\ge1$, define
$\varphi_n(e_i)=e_i-e_n$; let $\varphi_0$ be the zero map from $V_0=0$.
These maps are $S_n$-equivariant and injective, since the first $n$
coordinates of $\sum_i a_i(e_i-e_n)$ are the $a_i$. For $n\ge2$, $V_n$
is the direct sum of the trivial line and the irreducible sum-zero space
$S^{(n-1,1)}_k$, so its padded multiplicities are constant. To see the latter
identification directly, the $(n-1,1)$-tabloid module is the permutation
module on the singleton second row, and its polytabloids are the differences
$e_i-e_j$, which span the sum-zero space. Every image of $\varphi_n$ lies
in the sum-zero submodule of $V_{n+1}$, so its $S_{n+1}$-span misses the
trivial quotient. Thus (I) and (III) hold for $n\ge2$, while (II) fails. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Weight and stability degree give a uniform representation-stability range
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
with finite-dimensional values, weight $d:=\operatorname{weight}(V)<\infty$ and
stability degree $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]],
[[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). Let
$(V_n,\varphi_n)$ be the consistent sequence determined by $V$
([[def-uniform-representation-stability-for-consistent-sn-sequences]]). Then
$(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable with stable range
$n\ge d+s$: the maps $\varphi_n$ are injective for all $n\ge d+s$, the
$S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge d+s$, and
for every partition $\lambda$ the multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ of $V(\lambda)_n$
in $V_n$ is independent of $n$ for all $n\ge d+s$. No choice principle is
used.
items.strategy: Set $K_n=\ker\varphi_n\subseteq V_n$ and let $C_{n+1}$ be the cokernel of the $S_{n+1}$-map $\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{n+1}}_{S_n}\varphi_n\colon\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{n+1}}_{S_n}V_n\to V_{n+1}$; conditions (I) and (II) are exactly $K_n=0$ and $C_{n+1}=0$. Since $K_n$ is a subrepresentation of $V_n$ and $C_{n+1}$ a quotient of $V_{n+1}$, the coinvariant lemma (iv) reduces both to the vanishing of $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ for $n\ge d$. Exactness of $S_a$-coinvariants in characteristic $0$ identifies $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ with the kernel of $(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ with the cokernel of $(\operatorname{Ind}\varphi_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}$, and the transition map $T\colon\Phi_d(V)_{n-d}\to\Phi_d(V)_{n+1-d}$ factors through both, so it is the composite in the two ways displayed in the source. For $n-d\ge s$, $T$ is an isomorphism, so $(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ is injective and $(\operatorname{Ind}\varphi_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}$ is surjective; hence $K_n=0$ and $C_{n+1}=0$ for $n\ge s+d$. For (III), fix $m\le d$ and induct on $m=|\lambda|$: in the range $n\ge s+d$, decompose $(V_n)_{S_{n-m}}$ into constituents and use the coinvariant lemma (i) to see that only $|\lambda|\le m$ contribute, (iii) to see that the contributions of $|\lambda|<m$ are independent of $n$, and the induction hypothesis to see that their multiplicities are constant; the remaining summand is a direct sum of $\lambda$'s of size $m$ with multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ by (ii), so constancy of the total forces constancy of each $c_{\lambda,n}$. Here the range hypothesis enters twice: $\lambda_1\le s$ for every occurring constituent by the first-row bound, so $n\ge s+d\ge\lambda_1+m$ puts all constituents in the range where the coinvariant lemma applies, and the isomorphism statement of the stability degree applies at $n-m\ge s$.

items.title: Finite generation is equivalent to uniform representation stability
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
with finite-dimensional values
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). Then $V$ is finitely generated if and only
if the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ determined by $V$ is uniformly
representation stable
([[def-uniform-representation-stability-for-consistent-sn-sequences]],
[[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). No choice
principle is used.
items.strategy: ($\Rightarrow$) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le g$, then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$ by the generation-degree lemma (b), and the presentation lemma gives a surjection $M:=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{g}M(i)^{\oplus b_i}\twoheadrightarrow V$ with kernel $K$; by the Noetherian theorem $K$ is finitely generated, say in degree $\le r$. Exactness of $\Phi_a$ over $\mathbb Q$ writes $\Phi_a(V)\cong\Phi_a(M)/\Phi_a(K)$; the free summands have injectivity degree $0$ and $\operatorname{surj-deg}(K)\le r$, so $T$ is injective on $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ for $n\ge r$; hence $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)\le r$, $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)$ and the weight is finite. The preceding proposition then gives uniform representation stability in degrees $\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)+\operatorname{weight}(V)$. ($\Leftarrow$) If the sequence is uniformly representation stable for $n\ge N$, then for $n\ge N$ the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$, so the images of the finitely many $F I$-maps $V_n\to V_{n+1}$ span $V_{n+1}$; by induction $V=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le N})$, and since each $V_{\le N}$ is finite-dimensional by hypothesis, $V$ is finitely generated.

items.title: Character polynomials in the cycle counts $X_i$
items.statement: For $i\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ let $X_i\colon S_n\to\mathbb N$ be the class function sending a permutation to the number of its $i$-cycles ([[def-permutation-support-disjoint-cycles-and-cycle-type]]); thus $X_1(\sigma)$ is the number of fixed points. A **character polynomial** is a polynomial $P\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ in finitely many of the variables $X_i$, its **weighted degree** being defined by $\deg X_i:=i$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Since the class functions on $S_n$ form a $\mathbb Q$-algebra under pointwise multiplication ([[def-class-function-and-the-space-of-complex-class-functions]]), every character polynomial $P$ defines a class function $P\colon S_n\to\mathbb Q$ for every $n\ge0$. The expression is not unique on a single $S_n$, since $X_i$ vanishes identically for $i>n$; it is unique in the limit: if $P$ and $Q$ agree as functions on $S_n$ for infinitely many $n$, then $P=Q$. A sequence $(\chi_n)$ of class functions with $\chi_n$ a class function on $S_n$ is **eventually polynomial** when there are $N$ and a character polynomial $P$ with $\chi_n(\sigma)=P(\sigma)$ for all $n\ge N$ and all $\sigma\in S_n$.
items.strategy: Define the $X_i$ as class functions (they are constant on conjugacy classes because cycle type is a conjugacy invariant), define evaluation and weighted degree, and prove uniqueness by evaluating at permutations that fix all but a fixed finite set: for a monomial of top weighted degree $\le M$, the substitutions $X_1\mapsto n-c$, $X_r\mapsto X_r(\rho)$ for $r\ge2$ produce a polynomial in $n$; vanishing for infinitely many $n$ forces the coefficient of the top $X_1$-power to vanish on all fixed-point-free cycle types, and descending on the $X_1$-degree gives $P=0$. No representation theory is used in this definition.

items.title: Padded irreducible characters are eventually given by character polynomials
items.statement:
For every partition $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=m$ there is a character polynomial
$P_\lambda\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $m$
([[def-character-polynomial-in-cycle-counts]]) such that for every
$n\ge m+\lambda_1$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$

$$\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=P_\lambda\bigl(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots\bigr),$$

where $\lambda[n]=(n-m,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$ is the first-row padding
([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]) and $\chi^{\lambda[n]}$ is the
character of the irreducible Specht module $S^{\lambda[n]}$
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]]). No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Read five proof steps, eleven cited suppliers and complete local derivation. B_lambda counts fixed m-subsets by selected cycles and their Specht traces, with rational binomial coefficients and weighted degree <=m. Horizontal strips interlace, giving a fixed finite tail set E_lambda for n>=m+lambda_1. Its only size-m tail is lambda; every other tail has smaller size and its padding threshold is already met. Induction subtracts their polynomials; m=0 gives 1 and uniqueness follows on infinitely many ranks. Accept the complete independent replacement of the unsupported identity; no integral ordinary-coefficient claim or AC remains.

items.title: Finitely generated FI-modules have eventual character polynomials
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated
FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). Put
$d:=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$; both are
finite because $V$ is finitely generated
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]],
[[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). Then
there is a unique character polynomial $P_V\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of
weighted degree at most $d$ such that

$$\chi_{V_n}(\sigma)=P_V\bigl(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots\bigr)$$

for every $n\ge s+d$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$, where
$\chi_{V_n}(\sigma):=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma;V_n)$ is the character of the
$kS_n$-module $V_n$ ([[def-character-polynomial-in-cycle-counts]],
[[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]). No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: By the stability-range proposition applied to $V$, there are constants $c_\lambda\ge0$ with $V_n\cong\bigoplus_\lambda c_\lambda V(\lambda)_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, the sum over the finitely many $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|\le d$. For each such $\lambda$, $\lambda_1\le s$ by the first-row bound, so $n\ge s+d\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and the padded character polynomial lemma gives $\chi_{V(\lambda)_n}=P_\lambda$ of degree $\le|\lambda|$ on that range; additivity of characters gives $\chi_{V_n}=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda P_\lambda$, a character polynomial of weighted degree at most $d$ and with rational coefficients, as a function on all $S_n$ with $n\ge s+d$. Uniqueness: if two polynomials of weighted degree $\le d$ agree on $S_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, then by the uniqueness statement of the character-polynomial definition they are equal.

items.title: Each padded irreducible family is realised by a finitely generated FI-module
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\lambda$ be a partition with
$m:=|\lambda|$ and first part $\lambda_1$, and put $d:=m+\lambda_1$. For a
partition $\mu\vdash n$ write $V_\mu$ for the irreducible $kS_n$-module with
label $\mu$
([[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]),
and for $n\ge d$ let $\lambda[n]$ be the first-row padding of $\lambda$ to $n$
([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]).

Then there is a sub-FI-module $V(\lambda)$ of the free FI-module $M(\lambda)$
([[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]]) with

$$V(\lambda)_n\cong V_{\lambda[n]}\quad(n\ge d),\qquad V(\lambda)_n=0\quad(n<d),$$

so that the value of this FI-module at $[n]$ is the irreducible $kS_n$-module
denoted $V(\lambda)_n$ in [[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]].
This FI-module is generated in degree $\le d$
([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]), and its
generation degree is exactly $d$. It has

$$\operatorname{weight}(V(\lambda))=m,\qquad\operatorname{inj-deg}(V(\lambda))=0,\qquad\operatorname{surj-deg}(V(\lambda))=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V(\lambda))=\lambda_1,$$

where weight is as in [[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]] and the
three degrees are as in
[[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]. No
choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Put m=|lambda| and d=m+lambda_1. For n>=d, horizontal Pieri in M(lambda)_n gives the multiplicity-one constituent S^{lambda[n]}; take its canonical isotypic subspace and put V(lambda)_n=0 below d. For an injection f:[p]->[n] with p>=d, f_* is S_p-equivariant and its image is fixed by permutations of the complementary n-p points, since these permutations compose with f to f itself. Hence the image is a quotient of Ind_{S_p x S_{n-p}}^{S_n}(S^{lambda[p]} x 1). Any target shape nu in both this induced representation and M(lambda)_n satisfies nu_i>=lambda[p]_i for i>=2 and nu_{i+1}<=lambda_i by the two horizontal-strip interlacing conditions. Since lambda[p]_i=lambda_{i-1} for i>=2, these force nu_{i+1}=lambda_i for all i, i.e. nu=lambda[n]. Thus f_* preserves the selected subspaces; no map from the zero rank m space is used. Free-FI injection maps are injective on the direct sums indexed by image subsets, so a nonzero V(lambda)_d maps nontrivially at every n>=d; the S_n-span is the irreducible V(lambda)_n. Hence the family is generated in degree d and has weight m. Its injectivity degree is zero by containment in M(lambda). The evaluation map M(S^{lambda[d]}) -> V(lambda) is onto, and the exact free-module bound gives surjectivity degree at most lambda_1, because the first part of lambda[d] is lambda_1. At a=m, Phi_m(V(lambda))_{lambda_1} is nonzero while the previous graded piece is zero (when lambda_1>0), so the bound is sharp. For the empty partition, d=0 and the constant family has stability degree zero. All representations and interlacing arguments are finite-dimensional over the rational model, then extended to k; no field embeds into C.

items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d$ and stability degree $s$, with character polynomial $P_V$ as above. items.title: The padded family $V((2,1))$ begins at rank five, with weight three and stability degree two
items.statement:
Let $\lambda=(2,1)$, so $m:=|\lambda|=3$ and $\lambda_1=2$, and let
$\lambda[n]$ be the first-row padding
([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]). Then
$\lambda[n]=(n-3,2,1)$, and this is a partition exactly for

$$n\ge5=|\lambda|+\lambda_1:$$

for $n=3$ the sequence $(0,2,1)$ is not weakly decreasing, for $n=4$ the
sequence $(1,2,1)$ still is not, and for $n\ge5$ the first entry $n-3$ is at
least $\lambda_1=2$, so the sequence is a partition of $n$. The padded family
therefore begins at rank five, two ranks later than $|\lambda|=3$.

Accordingly, for a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, the FI-module
$V((2,1))$ of
[[prop-fi-module-realizing-one-padded-irreducible-family]] has values

$$V((2,1))_n\cong V_{(n-3,2,1)}\ (n\ge5),\qquad V((2,1))_n=0\ (n<5),$$

is generated in degree exactly $5$, and has
$\operatorname{weight}(V((2,1)))=3$ and
$\operatorname{inj-deg}(V((2,1)))=0$,
$\operatorname{surj-deg}(V((2,1)))=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V((2,1)))=2$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]],
[[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). For
instance $V((2,1))_5\cong V_{(2,2,1)}$, $V((2,1))_6\cong V_{(3,2,1)}$ and so
on: the first row grows while the second row stays at $2$. No choice principle
is used.
items.strategy: Check the padding threshold from the definition: $\lambda[n]$ is a partition iff $n-|\lambda|\ge\lambda_1$, i.e. $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1=5$; for $n=3,4$ the first part is smaller than the second, and for $n\ge5$ the sequence is weakly decreasing. Then apply the realization proposition, which gives generation in degree $5$, weight $|\lambda|=3$ and stability degree $\lambda_1=2$; the two divergences from the padding threshold $n=|\lambda|=3$ are exactly the point of the example.

items.title: A pointwise one-dimensional FI-module that is not finitely generated
items.statement:
**Refuted claim:** an FI-module over a field whose values $V_S$ are
finite-dimensional for every finite set $S$ is finitely generated.

The witness is built below: over a field $k$, take $V_S=k\,e_S$
one-dimensional for every finite set $S$, with bijections acting as the
identity identification of the lines and non-bijections acting as $0$. Then
$\dim_kV_S=1$ for all $S$, but no finite set of elements generates $V$
([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
items.strategy: Functoriality: composites of bijections are bijections and give the identity on $k e_S$, and if $f\circ g$ is a bijection then both $f$ and $g$ are bijections; so if either of $f,g$ fails to be a bijection, the composite $V(f)V(g)$ and $V(f\circ g)$ are both $0$. Non-finite-generation: given finitely many generating elements, choose $M$ at least as large as the sizes of the finite sets on which they live; every generator lies in some $V_S$ with $|S|\le M$, and every injection from such an $S$ into a set $T$ with $|T|>M$ is a non-bijection, so its image is $0$; hence the generated sub-FI-module is contained in $\bigoplus_{|T|\le M}V_T$ and misses $e_T$ for $|T|=M+1$. The pointwise spaces are one-dimensional, so pointwise finite generation (even finite-dimensionality) does not imply finite generation.

references.title: Thomas Church, Jordan S. Ellenberg and Benson Farb, “FI-modules and stability for representations of symmetric groups”, arXiv:1204.4533v4 (2014); published in Duke Math. J. 164 (2015) 1833–1910
